core_obligations: Record the three implications that are immediate from the definitions, namely (a) implies (b), (c) implies (a) and (d) implies (c) (proof lines 6583).

Assume the cofinal-system formulation and produce the inverse system: choose a compatible system of quotients with A_{n+1} modulo the image of J_n equal to A_n and with A the limit, and use cofinality to see that finite type holds at every stage (proof lines 6584-6603).

Lift generators of the first stage to elements of A, use the universal property of the restricted power series algebra to build a continuous map from it to A, and obtain surjectivity of its reductions modulo the ideals of definition (proof lines 6604-6619).

Form the short exact sequences given by those surjections, observe that the transition maps between the kernels are surjective, conclude that the inverse limit of the sequences is exact, and hence that the map from the restricted power series algebra to A is surjective and open with closed kernel -- which proves (b) implies (a) and closes the equivalence of (a) to (d) (proof lines 6620-6621).

For locality: given a diagram of the shape required by the situation, note that the two arrows to the completions satisfy the equivalent conditions by an example, reduce to the taut case, and consider the induced diagram between the quotients of the two arrows (proof lines 6623-6645).

Show the two directions needed for the axioms: finite type of one quotient map implies finite type of the other by the composition lemma, and, when the extension is faithfully flat, finite type of the second implies finite type of the first by descent of finite type along a faithfully flat etale map (proof lines 6645-6655).
Supply the verification of locality axiom (3), which the author declines to prove in this span (proof line 6656).
proof_roadmap: Inverse system of quotients and transfer of finite type (proof lines 6584-6603).
Lifting generators and constructing the map from the restricted power series algebra (proof lines 6604-6619).
Exactness of the inverse limit and surjectivity of the constructed map (proof lines 6620-6621).
Locality axioms (1) and (2) via the induced diagram on quotients (proof lines 6623-6655).
Locality axiom (3), omitted by the author (proof line 6656).
difficulty_reason: For an arrow of complete weakly admissible topological rings B to A, the lemma asserts the equivalence of four conditions -- tautness together with finite type of B/J to A/I for every weak ideal of definition, the same with a cofinal system of weak ideals of definition, tautness together with A being topologically of finite type over B, and A being isomorphic as a topological B-algebra to a quotient of a restricted power series algebra by a closed ideal -- and adds that these conditions define a local property, that is, they satisfy the three locality axioms (statement lines 6559-6580). Three of the implications are immediate from the definitions, and the substance is the implication from the cofinal-system formulation to the first one. That argument is a genuine construction: an inverse system of quotients A_n with A_{n+1} modulo the image of J_n equal to A_n and with A its limit is produced, finite generation is transferred downwards along the system, generators of the first stage are lifted to A, the universal property of the restricted power series algebra produces a continuous map to A, surjectivity of the induced maps on the quotients is obtained from a local nilpotence criterion, and the exactness of the inverse limit of the resulting short exact sequences -- using that the transition maps between the kernels are surjective -- shows that the map from the restricted power series algebra to A is surjective and open, with closed kernel (proof lines 6583-6620). The locality axioms (1) and (2) are then treated by a second, independent argument, in which the induced diagram between the quotients is shown to have etale horizontal maps and the two directions are read off from an algebra lemma and from the descent lemma for finiteness along a faithfully flat etale extension (proof lines 6622-6655). The claim is H3: the equivalence and the locality verification rest on different mechanisms, and the first of them requires an inverse-limit construction with an explicit Mittag-Leffler step.
